goal: Compare the methods reported in the three uploaded papers with experiment.xlsx results. Find the best configuration under 3M parameters, generate a chart, and assess whether our results support the reported design advantages. Use only uploaded data and documents; these are synthetic fixtures.
answer:
## Comparison and best under 3M

| Config | Params (M) | mIoU | Eligible <3M? |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| A (convolutional) | 2.5 | 73.27 | Yes — best eligible [Analysis 40f291f2-a2df-464d-a0ff-ee677d147797] |
| B (attention) | 3.2 | 76.0 | No — violates constraint [Analysis 40f291f2-a2df-464d-a0ff-ee677d147797] |
| C (compact conv baseline) | 2.0 | 70.0 | Yes [Analysis 40f291f2-a2df-464d-a0ff-ee677d147797] |

Fixture papers report Method A as convolutional segmentation (2.5M, 73.27) [paper_1.pdf, p.1], Method B as attention segmentation (3.2M, 76.0) [paper_2.pdf, p.1], and Method C as compact convolution baseline (2.0M, 70.0) [paper_3.pdf, p.1]. All three share the same fixture benchmark/protocol and the same A/B/C table [ev_83b29ad0340012b8e72d5080, ev_32b3846dd2dfd5109db37147, ev_0ada00d31c70b513af1e9075].

The `experiment.xlsx` dataset `8349454f...` has columns `model`, `params_m`, `miou` and sample rows A 2.5/73.27, B 3.2/76.0, C 2.0/70.0 [ev_987d289b187d46f2bb2916eef01c81ba, ev_40f291f2a2df464da0ffee677d147797]. These rows match the fixture table values [ev_83b29ad0340012b8e72d5080, ev_32b3846dd2dfd5109db37147, ev_0ada00d31c70b513af1e9075]. Thus, within the available sample, spreadsheet values are identical to the fixture values.

Computed `rank_under_budget` with `< 3.0M` gives eligible models A and C, and best = A (2.5M, 73.27) [Analysis 40f291f2-a2df-464d-a0ff-ee677d147797]. B is 3.2M and must be excluded despite its higher mIoU [Analysis 40f291f2-a2df-464d-a0ff-ee677d147797]. The chart output is named `comparison.png` [Analysis 40f291f2-a2df-464d-a0ff-ee677d147797].

## Support for reported design advantages

The papers report descriptive deltas: A over C +3.27 mIoU at +0.5M params; B over A +2.73 mIoU at +0.7M params [ev_83b29ad0340012b8e72d5080, ev_32b3846dd2dfd5109db37147, ev_0ada00d31c70b513af1e9075]. They explicitly state these are synthetic test values, not published research claims, with descriptive quality/cost tradeoff only and no causal or ablation claim [paper_3.pdf, p.1]. There are no uncertainty estimates [paper_3.pdf, p.1].

Because `experiment.xlsx` contains the same synthetic fixture rows, it is consistent with those descriptive deltas, but it does not independently validate them. Under `<3M`, only the A-over-C advantage is selectable; B’s higher mIoU is outside budget [Analysis 40f291f2-a2df-464d-a0ff-ee677d147797]. Therefore, the available data support the description that A improves over C within budget, but do not support selecting B or claiming a causal design advantage.

## Limits and unresolved items

- The ranked list places B first despite the `<3M` constraint; the same output’s eligible/best fields resolve selection to A [Analysis 40f291f2-a2df-464d-a0ff-ee677d147797].
- No direct side-by-side paper-vs-spreadsheet mapping artifact is present in the cited evidence; comparison rests on identical sample rows [ev_987d289b187d46f2bb2916eef01c81ba, ev_40f291f2a2df464da0ffee677d147797, ev_83b29ad0340012b8e72d5080, ev_32b3846dd2dfd5109db37147, ev_0ada00d31c70b513af1e9075].
